articleTitle: UML Functional Aspects in Business-to-Business: Some Lessons Learned
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: In the early stages of software development, identifying, addressing, and resolving design issues is crucial to enhancing software quality and reducing costs. Techniques such as use case modeling and Unified Modeling Language (UML) scenario engineering have gained prominence in the elicitation of requirements, specification development, and the creation and interpretation of design documents. In recent years, Business-to-Business (B2B) collaboration has emerged as a key driver for the success of modern enterprises, especially within the rapidly evolving e-business landscape. Although various Business-to-Business protocols have been designed to facilitate these interactions, a universally accepted standard has yet to emerge. UML has played a significant role in the development of business information systems. This paper presents insights and best practices for applying UML scenario engineering in creating sequence diagrams, scenario extension, and developing Business-to-Business systems.

articleTitle: Study of motor oil adulteration employing a novel neural network approach for processing laser-induced fluorescence spectra
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: In recent years, Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) have been increasingly applied to process spectroscopic data due to their ability to produce highly accurate non-linear models. This work aims to use Laser Induced Fluorescence (LIF) spectroscopy and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) for two purposes: the first is to classify high-grade motor oil adulterated by three lower-grade motor oils depending on the type of adulterant and the second is to predict the adulteration percentage of high-grade motor oil by the other oils. Feature selection algorithm was applied to extract and identify optimal wavelengths from the raw spectra. Among the 534 wavelengths extracted, 164 have been selected as the most suitable features for the ANN model. The study demonstrated that using feature selection with ANN improved model performance over using the original spectra. The best regression model was obtained using an ANN with structure 164-6-6-10-1, yielding a prediction regression coefficient ($\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{p}}$) of $\mathbf{0. 9 9}$ and a prediction Root Mean Square Error (RMSE ${ }_{p}$) of $\mathbf{1. 6 6 \%}$. For classification, $\mathbf{1 0 0 \%}$ accuracy was achieved in all three learning phases: training, validation and testing. As a result, ANNs have proven their ability to process LIF data with high accuracy. Combining LIF and ANN is an efficient, fast and non-destructive method for qualitative and quantitative analysis of engine oil adulteration.

articleTitle: Enhancing News Credibility Detection in Arabic: A Study of Attentional Bidirectional LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Detecting fake news continues to be a major challenge in the digital era, especially in languages with significant linguistic diversity such as Arabic, which is highly ambiguous, morphologically rich, and has numerous dialects. This study presents an enhanced method for detecting Arabic fake news by leveraging an Attentional Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (AttBiLSTM) model. Our proposed model integrates an attentional mechanism with BiLSTM to improve classification accuracy. Evaluated on the benchmark AFND Fake News dataset, our approach demonstrates significant improvements in identifying news credibility, achieving an accuracy of $\mathbf{7 9 . 2 0 \%}$. This research advances deep learning methods for fake news detection by offering an effective solution tailored to Arabic language contexts.

articleTitle: Enhanced approach for performance analysis in Vehicular Communications leveraging Taguchi and ANOVA methods
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: In Vehicular communications, routing the information efficiently and accurately is still a major concern for many researchers, owing to the high mobility of vehicles, the frequent changes in the network topology and the security vulnerabilities. In that regard, the present work aims at analyzing the influence of scalability, connectivity and routing attacks on routing protocols in vehicular communications, by applying two statistical approaches: The Taguchi Method and ANOVA analysis. The Taguchi Method is used to design the experiments by means of an L8 Orthogonal Array, the obtained experiment results were then analyzed using Taguchi Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) analysis. Additionally, ANOVA method was implemented in order to consolidate the analysis and confirm the findings of the Taguchi Method. The current study considers investigating the effect of four factors on Throughput, Average delay, Packet Loss, and Overhead. We selected NS-3 as a Network Simulator and SUMO for generating a realistic vehicular mobility model. The implementation of Taguchi Method enabled to simultaneously discern the effect of factors and possible interactions on the considered responses, through a reduced number of experiments. Moreover, the ANOVA method helped in determing the contribution and the statistical significance of the different investigated factors.

articleTitle: Enhancing Microblogging User Recommendations using BERT-based Transformer and LDA Topic Models
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Microblogging systems, that enable users to submit their entries and follow other microbloggers who share their interests, have seen enormous success. The followee suggestion assignment has received increased attention in the last few years. Actually, it takes much time and effort to identify users who share your interests because of the massive volume of information that users provide every day. As a result, the requirement for a system to help consumers locate this information becomes essential. In this research, we present a followee recommender system to help users discover microbloggers who share their interests. Furthermore, the BERT model for language modeling, the Latent Dirichlet Allocation model for modeling, and the Long Short Term Memory model for predictions from the basis of our methodology. We execute in-depth tests using an offline dataset that was obtained from Twitter (Currently X platforms) to demonstrate the efficiency of our approach. The outcomes of the experiment demonstrate that our method beats the latest techniques in terms of recall and precision.

articleTitle: Stock Market Volatility Forecasting: A Supervised Learning Approach with Normal Tempered λ-Stable Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: In the domain of supervised learning in finance, numerous empirical studies consistently highlight the prevalence of fat-tailed distributions in financial volatility series. This study introduces an innovative approach to estimate stock market return volatility using Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (ARCH) models. The focus is on the normal tempered λ-stable law, which offers enhanced flexibility for statistical analysis compared to the fixed variance associated with the normal law. The normal tempered λ-stable law is particularly noteworthy as it integrates the advantageous features of the tempered λ-stable law while maintaining well-defined moments. Our empirical findings strongly support the proposition that ARCH models employing the normal tempered λ-stable law deliver superior predictive outcomes for stock market volatility estimation, outperforming both the normal and Student distributions. This advancement underscores the potential of supervised learning techniques in improving financial volatility forecasting.

articleTitle: State of the Art on CAN Protocol Vulnerabilities and Intrusion Detection Systems in Automotive Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The Controller Area Network (CAN) protocol is a primary communication protocol in modern vehicles that enables communication among electronic control units (ECU). Nevertheless, this protocol contains numerous weaknesses that make automotive networks susceptible to various cyber dangers, including message spoofing, eavesdropping, and denial-of-service (DoS) assaults. This article provides a detailed analysis of modern Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) created to protect CAN networks. We evaluated and contrasted the most recent IDS approaches, discussing their advantages and disadvantages. The paper points out the current research limitations and suggests potential future research directions to improve IDS performance in automotive networks. The practical implications of these discoveries suggest that employing IDS methodologies in real-world settings could greatly enhance the security of modern vehicles.

articleTitle: Analysis of Moroccan Arabic Speech Recognition for Integration in Voice Command Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems transform acoustic waveforms into corresponding text representations, effectively capturing the semantic content conveyed by speakers. This paper presents the development of an ASR system tailored to Moroccan Arabic (Darija) for recognizing connected words in command-and-control scenarios. The system was trained on a dataset consisting of 2,394 words, each repeated 10 times, articulated by 19 speakers (both male and female) in Moroccan Arabic. It leverages the CMU Sphinx toolkit and employs Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) integrated with Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) for acoustic modeling. Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) were used for feature extraction. Experimental results demonstrate a recognition accuracy of $\mathbf{9 3 . 3 3 \%}$ for connected words, achieved using a configuration with four Gaussian mixtures.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN Model Architecture with Data Augmentation for Intelligent Arabic Handwritten Character Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Text recognition in handwritten Arabic scripts is a dynamic research field, but one that also faces various significant challenges such as managing vast open databases and the infinite variability of writing styles. In our study, we set out to address these specific challenges by exploring a deep learning architecture for the recognition of handwritten Arabic characters. Our approach was structured around two distinct models. Firstly, we developed a standalone CNN model, leveraging the intrinsic capabilities of this architecture for detecting complex patterns. Subsequently, we investigated a hybrid CNN model, integrating SVM, Random Forest, and XGBoost techniques, while also leveraging data augmentation to enhance the robustness of our system. The evaluations we conducted highlighted the remarkable performance of the hybrid CNN model, coupled with the Random Forest classifier, surpassing other approaches with an accuracy reaching $98 \%$. To ensure the reliability of our results, we took measures to protect our models against overfitting, using the dropout technique and conducting a thorough analysis of relevant metrics. The performance of our model was assessed on the AHCD database, comprising 16,800 letters, and compared to that of other state-of-the-art approaches in Arabic text recognition. The results of our study demonstrate the superiority of our approach, thus offering new perspectives in the field of handwritten Arabic character recognition.

articleTitle: Advanced Optimization of Discrete Orthogonal Hahn Moments for Precision Image Reconstruction via the Firefly Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: In recent decades, discrete orthogonal moments have frequently been used to represent images in a variety of computer vision and pattern recognition applications. These moments commonly employ discrete orthogonal polynomials as their basis, some of which are parametric and characterized by localization parameters. Optimizing these parameters is crucial for enhancing the efficiency of orthogonal moments in image analysis. This paper takes a new approach for optimizing the discrete Hahn polynomial parameters ($\alpha, \beta$) using the Firefly optimization algorithm, focusing on minimizing the mean square reconstruction error. Where our method identifies the optimal $\alpha$ and $\beta$ values for constructing Hahn polynomials to achieve superior image moments. The results demonstrate that our Firefly algorithm-based method significantly improves image reconstruction quality, yielding lower reconstruction errors, particularly in low orders of Hahn moments. Furthermore, the proposed method outperforms both the artificial bee colony optimization method and the standard parameter selection method. The experiments clearly indicate the advantages of our proposed method, especially in the lower orders of moments.

articleTitle: Enhancing Recruitment Transparency and Efficiency with Explainable AI (XAI)
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: In an era where data-driven decision-making is paramount, recruitment processes increasingly leverage advanced algorithms to enhance efficiency and effectiveness. However, the complexity and opacity of these machine learning models often create difficulties in understanding and trusting their predictions. This paper explores how Explainable AI (XAI) can bridge this gap, specifically based on two key techniques: Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME). By applying these XAI methods to recruitment data, we aim to unravel the underlying factors influencing hiring decisions and improve the transparency of the process.

articleTitle: Enhancing encryption of an RGB image by combining the Lorenz chaotic system and Arnold’s cat map
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The encryption of an RGB image can be significantly improved by combining the Lorenz chaotic system with Arnold’s cat map, leveraging the strengths of both chaotic systems to achieve robust image security. The Lorenz system, known for its complex and unpredictable behavior, can be employed to generate a sequence of pseudorandom numbers used for key-based pixel shuffling. The result is then utilized to drive Arnold’s map, which excels at spatially rearranging pixel positions through its chaotic stretch-and-fold transformation. By first applying the Lorenz system to produce a dynamic key stream and then using Arnold’s cat map to permute pixel positions, this combined approach enhances encryption by introducing multiple layers of complexity and unpredictability. The Lorenz system’s sensitivity to initial conditions ensures that even small changes in the key lead to significantly different transformations, while the Arnold cat map’s mixing properties ensure that pixel values are thoroughly scrambled. The result is an image that is exceptionally resistant to both statistical analysis and brute-force attacks, providing a higher level of security for sensitive visual data.

articleTitle: Robust Control of Mechanical Systems Applied on Vehicle Active Suspension System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Robustness analysis of mechanical system performance generally aims to identify whether the system performs as predicted for expected parameter variations. The main objective of robust control is to keep the closed loop stable and ensure a certain level of performance, but also to reduce the sensitivity of the control structure in the presence of parametric variations and possible disturbances affecting the model of the system to be controlled. In this work, we have analyzed robustness and applied robust control to solve the problem of automatic control of a vehicle’s active suspension. In order to evaluate the impact of uncertain parameters on the performance of the system under study, several simulations have been presented.

articleTitle: SDN and NFV security approaches for IoT environments
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The application of the Internet of Things (IoT) in several fields introduces a lack of protection level and opens new gaps for cybercriminals. Current security mechanisms are not adapted to the dynamic characteristics of IoT and are not capable of answering its requirements. In this sense, Software Defined Networking (SDN) and Network Function Virtualization (NFV) are two new concepts that can be used to reinforce the cybersecurity of IoT systems. For this reason, we propose, in this paper, a deep analysis and comprehensive study of different security mechanisms introduced by SDN and NFV and its impact on addressing IoT security challenges, and we compare them with conventional security mechanisms. Then, we discuss the several challenges related to applying SDN and NFV in IoT security functionalities.

articleTitle: Theoretical Study and Simulation of Two Radiometers for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: A malignant tumor’s internal temperature is a reliable indicator of the tumor’s rate of growth. Based on this principle, this research explores the use of microwave radiometry, a technique that measures the thermal power emitted by human tissues, as a potential diagnostic tool for breast cancer. The study presents a theoretical analysis and MATLAB simulation of two microwave radiometer designs—the total power radiometer and the dicke radiometer—tailored for non-invasive breast tissue temperature measurement. Operating in the 2 to 4 GHz frequency range, this passive microwave radiometer is designed to detect temperature variations at specific depths, enabling the identification of malignancies. By comparing the two circuit designs, this work aims to assess their performance in terms of sensitivity, circuit complexity, and noise to determine the optimal approach for clinical application.

articleTitle: An Algorithm for Image Encryption Combining the Lorenz System, XOR Operation, and Inverted Bit Permutation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This paper proposes a new image encoding algorithm that integrates inverted bit permutation with the chaotic behavior of a hybrid Lorenz chaotic system and XOR operation. The method capitalizes on the inherent of the three-dimensional Lorenz system to produce a highly unpredictable key employed to improve both the encryption process’s security and efficiency. This approach offers various advantages: the high resistance to cryptographic attacks, scalability, and use for different image types. The experimental finding confirm the performance and dependability of the suggested encryption technique and prove to be an effective procedure for secure image transmission and storage.

articleTitle: Comparison between 2D Classification and 3D Classification based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The rise in processing power of computers and the availability of a considerable amount of data have allowed the overlap of several machine learning approaches. This has led to breakthroughs on many deep learning tasks as speech recognition, natural language processing (NLP), object detection and image analysis. Thus, many fields as autonomous driving, industrial quality processes and mobile robotic have released multiples researches in deep learning algorithmic topics. In this paper, we have made a comparison, in terms of accuracy and process timing, between classifications based on 3D points cloud and 2D images for the same input dataset in raw format, and generated basic outlines of both deep learning methods using algorithms based on convolution networks. We discovered that 3D points cloud based classification model was slow on training stage than 2D images model timing due to the 3D complexity data representation. Besides that, classification neural networks based on 3D points cloud data performed better on accuracy than the networks based on 2D images datasets. It is to highlight that 3D based systems are so critical in terms of data processing compared to 2D images due to: Data format as points cloud, meshes and volumes, the hardware resources requirement which is higher due to the third added dimension. Finally, we hypothesize that systems which would combine both of these data geometry and networks architectures would return accuracy better and low processing time wise.

Author Keywords: 2D images data and Convolution Neuronal networks

articleTitle: Artificial intelligence in Quality4.0
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Many studies, mostly based on different sectors applying Industry 4.0, do not highlight the role of artificial intelligence in those sectors and particularly in quality management. Though an appropriate amount of research regarding the implementation of Quality 4.0 has advanced, which is the evolution of quality management systems pertaining to technological alignment with Industry 4.0 technologies, it is mostly within the confined applications of a single sector. It has narrowed the general knowledge of how AI could really improvise processes of quality across different industries. This broad paper takes such a scope in aiming to assess the incorporation of AI in Quality 4.0 from a cross-sectoral view with a perspective to learn how advanced machine learning, predictive analytics, and real-time data analytics can help polish quality management systems. The emphasis is placed upon the manner in which AI could assist an industry to manage large amounts of data, improve production efficiency, and forestall issue through proactive steps such as anomaly detection and predictive maintenance. With this study, by considering the prospect of AI in varied economic sectors, new doorways are unlocked for creative quality management practices. Our study attempts to establish that transformative potential of AI for process optimization under Quality 4.0 approaches that make them skillful, effective, and adaptive to rapidly evolving requirements in today’s industrial setup. Therefore, it offers an insight into how AI can complement Quality 4.0 toward leading the future of industrial operations with the wider vision of Industry 4.0 while ensuring that the industries are coming up with even better solutions to cope with the complexities of the new production setups.

articleTitle: Two-Teacher Net: Dual-Distillation-Based QAT for CNN Compression
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Accelerating Vision Transformers (ViT) for image classification have demonstrated remarkable performance in various computer vision tasks, often surpassing the capabilities of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). However, their high computational requirements and large number of parameters have limited their efficiency for edge computing inference. This paper introduces “Two-Teachers Net,” a novel CNN compression technique that combines Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) with dual-teacher Knowledge Distillation (2-KD) using a modified Cross-Entropy Loss function to learn complex features from smaller datasets compared to transformer architectures. Our method was trained on three-phases and was validated with CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets on EfficientNet, RegNet, and ConvNeXt architectures. This approach resulted in improving the accuracy for the quantized 8 -bit student model by $\mathbf{1 - 2 \%}$ over existing compression solutions. The proposed method can work with various CNNs architectures and seamlessly integrates with AI optimization toolchains like Vitis-AI, OpenVINO, and ONNX without architectural adjustments, enabling real-time inference and high-accuracy predication on the edge for applications like medical imaging and ADAS.

articleTitle: Advanced 3D Color Image Encryption Using Lorenz and Rössler Chaotic Systems:A Multi-Layered Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This work introduces a new approach to 3D image encryption using Lorenz and Rössler maps. These two chaotic systems are employed to generate secure and unpredictable keys for the encryption process. The Lorenz map, known for its sensitivity to initial conditions and complex attractor, is combined with the Rössler map, another chaotic system with distinct dynamic properties. By integrating these two three-dimensional chaotic maps, the proposed method enhances the security and robustness of image encryption. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through various encryption and decryption tests, which show its potential to protect sensitive visual data against unauthorized access and attacks. Experimental results, including histograms and correlation coefficients, validate the effectiveness and reliability of the suggested method for ensuring secure image encryption suitable for transmission and storage applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Photovoltaic Maintenance with Real-Time Data Integration: A Sensorless And Scalable Approach Validated By Intelligent Correlation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative and cost-effective approach to gathering, storing and managing photovoltaic and meteorological data, avoiding the use of traditional sensors, wires and cables. Conventionally, systems for data collection often require costly tools as well as sophisticated cabling networks; they revolve around the same methodologies with difficult setups and complicated maintenance needs, which can limit their application, long-term reliability and scalability in countries with budget constraints and challenging environmental conditions such as Morocco. The presented solution leverages built-in functionalities of photovoltaic inverters to collect crucial data such as real-time generated power, current, voltage and consumed energy. Regarding weather parameters, a set of online open-source techniques has been explored to compile all necessary data required by the researchers, especially those working merely with simulated metrics, to successfully carry out their projects. Machine learning models have been developed to forecast PV power and verify the accuracy of the data, showing a high degree of correlation with inverter-based information. Particularly, decision tree regression and support vector regression were employed. The results on the test sets were as follows: the decision tree regression model achieved a mean squared error of 0.2199 and an $\mathbf{R}^{2}$ score of 0.7769, while the support vector regression model presented a mean squared error of 0.0936 and a higher $\mathbf{R}^{2}$ score of 0.9051. In the end, an online accessible dashboard that showcases important graphs and includes a notification center to alert users as the need arises has been designed, representing a significant step forward in the quest for photovoltaic system maintenance excellence.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Low Energy Consumption Data Logger for a Nano-Grid Applied to a Solar Smart Greenhouse
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: In response to growing environmental concerns and the necessity for sustainable development, this paper explores the integration of renewable energy technology with advanced agricultural practices. We present the design and implementation of a low energy consumption data logger for a nano-grid tailored to a solar-powered smart greenhouse. This system embodies the convergence of sustainability and technology, enhancing both energy management and agricultural productivity. Utilizing a standalone photovoltaic (PV) system, the smart greenhouse operates self-sufficiently, reducing its carbon footprint. The nano-grid, comprising PV panels, battery storage, and load management, ensures year-round renewable energy supply. The data logger monitors environmental parameters within the greenhouse, as well as metrics from the PV system, and its low energy design minimizes power consumption, maintaining overall system efficiency. The deployment of a wireless sensor network within the greenhouse further enhances scalability and real-time monitoring capabilities, directly impacting crop quality and yield. This paper details the system architecture, addresses integration challenges, and evaluates the data logger’s performance, contributing valuable insights to the field of sustainable agricultural practices through renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: Efficient implementation of codebook algorithm for background subtraction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Background subtraction is a critical component of numerous image processing applications, particularly in video surveillance. Considerable effort has been devoted to enhancing the accuracy of codebook algorithms. However, these improvements have led to significant increases in computing power requirements, rendering them impractical for real-time applications. The performances of codebook algorithms are mainly due to its inherent complexity and the variable number of codewords dedicated to represents each pixel. Which requires frequent memory allocation and deallocation. To address these limitations, we propose optimizing the codebook model in order to reduce its size while preserving accuracy and enabling real-time processing.

articleTitle: Moroccan Arabic Darija Automatic Speech Recognition System using CNN Model for Drone Control Application
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) system using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model to control drone movements through Moroccan Arabic Darija commands. The system leverages Mel Spectrogram features to extract robust speech patterns and is evaluated using a customized corpus of 6,160 tokens on a high-spec laptop. Additionally, a comparative analysis of activation functions was conducted to assess their impact on model performance. Experimental results demonstrate the system’s effectiveness and real-time suitability, achieving an accuracy rate of 97.27% and a recognition time of 170 milliseconds.

articleTitle: Adaptive Genetic Algorithm for 2D Problems With a Dynamic Gene Walk
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The genetic algorithm is one of the most commonly used metaheuristics due to its adaptability to various types of problems. However, its implementation can be challenging because of the hyperparameters, especially when the objective function has few parameters. In this paper, we demonstrate the limitations of the genetic algorithm in 2D problems and introduce a new algorithm called the Adapted Genetic Algorithm. This algorithm uses a dynamic walk instead of mutation. The dynamic walk is a custom step in the 2D space that chromosomes take in the direction that most improves the objective function. This dynamic walk can be modified depending on the problem, ranging from a simple constant to a complex trigonometric function. We tested the Adapted Genetic Algorithm on four 2D functions: the parabola, Griewank, Rastrigin, and Ackley. All tests showed the superiority of our adapted algorithm compared to the simulated annealing, artificial bee colony, particle swarm optimization, and the classic genetic algorithm.

articleTitle: Improved Polar Lights Optimizer Algorithm using Chaotic Maps for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This paper presents an improvement of the Polar Lights Optimizer (PLO) algorithm by integrating three chaotic maps. A dynamic diversification method based on chaotic systems enables the enhanced algorithm, known as Chaotic Polar Light Optimizer (CPLO), to better escape local minima and converge to globally optimal solutions. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed CPLO algorithm, we selected four test functions and a real problem, namely the segmentation of medical images. The performance of CPLO was compared with that of the PLO algorithm and three other well-known algorithms. Experimental findings validate the suggested algorithm’s robustness and efficacy in real-world situations while demonstrating improved convergence time and solution quality.

articleTitle: Enhancing Analysis by Integrating Link and Node Metrics based Fuzzy Logic for IoT System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has recently emerged as a transformative paradigm driven by technological advancements. Networks comprised of connected devices face numerous challenges, particularly in facilitating communication among these devices. These challenges arise due to the inherent constraints of IoT, such as limited power and the nature of Low Power and Lossy Networks (LLNs). LLNs require an efficient routing protocol that can cater to the needs of diverse applications while managing these constraints effectively. Over the past few years, The IETF ROLL (Routing Over Low Power and Lossy Networks) working group has developed a new routing protocol, RPL (IPv6 Routing Protocol for LLNs). RPL leverages objective functions to construct and optimize routing paths to ensure efficient data transmission within LLNs. Nevertheless, the IETF ROLL group did not specify the exact number or types of metrics to be employed in these objective functions, leaving room for customization based on specific application requirements. This study delves into the RPL routing protocol, examining its structure and functionality. Furthermore, we propose a novel objective function that integrates multiple metrics to enhance routing performance. The integration of these metrics is accomplished through fuzzy logic, enabling a more flexible and nuanced approach to decision-making in the routing process. This method aims to improve the overall efficiency and reliability of data transmission within LLNs, addressing the unique challenges posed by IoT environments.

articleTitle: Optimizing Direct Power Control of Variable Speed Wind Turbine Systems Using Genetic Algorithms and Space Vector Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This writing examines the implementation of a genetic algorithm (GA) for optimizing direct power control in variable speed wind turbine systems based on doubly-fed induction generators (DFIGs). This method is a linear control technique with a quicker response and simple structure, but it has some limitations in terms of power quality as well as robustness against parameter variations. What makes DPC-GA unique is its reliance on a GA to establish the best control parameters for DPC, which results in reduced power ripple, minimized current harmonic distortion, and improved system robustness. To apply the new technology named DPC-GA into this system, an SVM-based space vector modulation was implemented into the paper. The simulation results have shown that DPC-GA outperforms other conventional Direct Power Controls by giving an indication that it has high potential for energy saving and wind energy production at a large scale.

articleTitle: CSHA-CSI: Towards Contactless Sensing of Human Activities Utilizing WiFi Channel State Information
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Numerous studies have demonstrated the interest of reusing wireless signals (such as WiFi) for detecting human activity and therefore realizing numerous innovative applications, including security surveillance, daily activity tracking, monitoring vital signs, and identifying users, which require more precise motion detection. Such solutions may facilitate a broad spectrum of uses for smart homes and offices, encompassing security, healthcare monitoring and management, intelligent healthcare solutions, and smart appliance interaction. Through the analysis of the wireless signals that have been received, it is possible to detect human motions due to the effects that human movements exert on the transmission of wireless signals (including phenomena like reflection, diffraction, and scattering). Wireless sensing of human activity has gained significant interest in recent years and emerged as a critical field of research due to its low cost and non-intrusiveness. In this study, we introduce a non-invasive as well as robust system to recognize human activity, utilizing affordable and widely used WiFi devices, eliminating the need for individuals to don or transport items. Our system also has the capability for extensive deployment and continuous longterm monitoring. Experimental results demonstrate the reliability as well as the precision of our system within realistic settings. This is a clear indication that non-invasive, continuous fine-grained human activity monitoring is feasible without incurring additional costs.

articleTitle: Conception of the C19H2RM-2 prototype based on an embedded camera module for driver state monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This paper presents the C16H2RM-2 prototype, designed using AutoCAD and representing a cutting-edge solution for monitoring driver health metrics, including heart rate, breathing rate, and signs of fatigue. The protoptype was based on a first version C16H2RM that uses mainly the raspberry pi 4 board. The system integrates photoplethysmography (PPG) sensors, which are strategically positioned to accurately measure physiological parameters. The AutoCAD-designed enclosure, crafted from durable and transparent plexiglass, houses the Jetson Nano plateform, the fan, the LED and the uninterruptible power supply module (UPS). The prototype enhances both the accuracy of data collection and the ease of use, aiming to improve driver safety and reduce fatigue-related incidents on the road.

articleTitle: Towards Blockchain Technology for Enhancing Agri-IoT Security
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) into agriculture, commonly referred to as Agri-IoT, has significantly improved the efficiency and productivity of modern agriculture. However, the widespread deployment of IoT devices presents security challenges, such as data breaches, unauthorized access, and cyber-attacks, compromising agricultural data integrity. Blockchain technology, with its features of decentralization, transparency, and immutability, offers a promising solution to enhance data integrity, reduce manipulation risks, and promote trust among stakeholders. The purpose of this work is to explore blockchain’s potential for enhancing the security of Agri-IoT systems and provide a roadmap for further research to develop secure, scalable, and resilient solutions to safeguard the future of agriculture.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Perceptual Hashing Algorithms for Digital Image Authenticity
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The authenticity and integrity of digital images have become paramount in an era of advanced editing tools and widespread manipulation. To address the challenges of detecting tampered images, this research provides a thorough examination of six perceptual hashing techniques. A-Hash, DHash, P-Hash, W-Hash, SVD-Hash, PDQ-Hash. Unlike existing studies that primarily focus on isolated methods, this work provides a comparative analysis to determine their effectiveness in identifying complex tampering approaches such as copy-move and splicing manipulations, using the CASIA V2 dataset.The original contribution of this study lies in its systematic assessment of these algorithms based on three key criteria: robustness to perceptual variations, capacity for discrimination, and authentication ability, measured using the normalized Hamming distance metric.This work not only offers valuable insights into the strengths and weaknesses of perceptual hashing techniques but also serves as a foundational reference for advancing digital forensics and enhancing the reliability of image authentication systems.

articleTitle: Universal design of an Embedded Hardware for Educational robotics based on Atmega328P
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of an universal and cost-effective embedded hardware platform for educational robotics applications. The core of the system utilizes the popular Atmega328P microcontroller, known for its robustness and affordability. The design prioritizes minimalism principles while maintaining essential functionalities for basic robot control and sensors integration. The hardware system includes four stepper motor drivers, four H-bridge motor drivers, a 16-channel PWM controller and GPIO connections for sensors and user command. The software design provides a versatile framework for controlling motors, reading sensor data, and enabling communication between devices, making the platform easy to program and customize. Our design makes the system ideal for educational and research settings, allowing users to explore robotics concepts without the constraints of complex and expensive hardware.

articleTitle: Region-Wise Weather Data-Based Crop Recommendation Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Annually, numerous agricultural crops suffer significant losses due to insufficient technical knowledge and unpredictable weather patterns, including fluctuations in precipitation, temperature, and other environmental conditions crucial for crop yield and profitability. Selecting appropriate crops to enhance yield is vital for improving real-life farming scenarios. In this context, crop recommendation systems leveraging IoT data in smart agriculture have emerged as invaluable tools in modern farming practices. These systems increasingly utilize machine learning techniques to determine the most adequate crops based on continuously measured soil, environmental, and weather parameters collected by IoT sensors. This manuscript investigates the integration of cutting-edge machine learning algorithms for crops selection, employing an open dataset of 2200 data points covering 22 crops. We compare the performance of Gaussian Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Extra Trees Classifier, Decision Trees, Logistic Regression, k-Nearest Neighbors and Support Vector Machines in determining suitable crops based on soil and weather parameters. Our results demonstrate notable improvements in the accuracy of crop selection, with Gaussian Naive Bayes achieving an accuracy of 99.82%, outperforming other algorithms in both accuracy and computational efficiency. This approach offers a viable solution to empower farmers with tools for improved farm productivity and sustainable agriculture. Finally, we discuss the potential impact of these systems on sustainable farming practices.

articleTitle: A Rich and Balanced MSA Corpus for HMM-Based Consonant-Vowel Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This research delves into the creation of an innovative Modern Standard Arabic corpus, aiming for a comprehensive balance and richness while adhering to Zipf’s law. Building a phonetically diverse Arabic sentence collection yields significant advantages in terms of efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and storage capacity compared to conventional corpora. The corpus currently contains 527 sentences from various resources, the word forms generated are rich and balanced, and it contains all phonemes of the Arabic language. The sentences and expressions verify the laws of balanced phonetic distribution. We integrate with this study Hidden Markov Model (HMM) applying to analyze the underlying structure of created corpus. Indeend, HMM method is used to confirm consonant - vowels segmentation, in the corpus. We train our system by re-estimation of HMM parameters to have the maximum probability of observing Arabic symbols using Forward, Backward and Baum-Welch Algorithms. The obtained results indicate that, the distinction between consonants and vowels is a statistically significant feature inherent in the Arabic language.

articleTitle: Accurate Real-World Co-ordinate Finding and the Object Classification for the Robot Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This paper presents an object detection and classification of the objects using Deep Learning (DL). The integration of object detection algorithms and depth camera developed is capable of providing robots, such as self developed assistive intelligent robot called “ROSWITHA” (RObot System WITH Autonomy) with the ability to detect an object and interpret their surrounding environment. It also provides the real-world coordinates/position of the object in that environment, which helps the robot to perform some applications, such as grabbing and serving, etc. You Only Look Once (YOLO) is one of the most popular object detection algorithms which is treated as a single regression problem and is processed by a single neural network. In this work, the YOLOv5 (YOLO version 5) network is implemented on a depth camera “RealSense” for processing object detection and estimating the position of the objects. The model is trained on reduced/filtered application-required objects (e.g. bottle and cup) from the available COCO dataset, and the training outcome alongside the performance of the overall system was evaluated. The results exhibited a satisfactory performance of the model in accurately detecting and classifying the objects with a high confidence score ranging from the least to $\mathbf{7 2 \%}$ to the highest of $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$. The confidence score could also be adjusted by the user on the developed GUI to attain the most certain predictions.

articleTitle: Strengthening Security in the Internet of Things (IoT): Integrated Approach of Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) and Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) applications has led to an increase in sophisticated and malicious attacks, threatening network security and privacy in sectors such as healthcare, industry, and home automation. To address these challenges, The implementation of Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) has become crucial for detecting and mitigating these threats. At the same time, the emergence of Edge Computing technology offers significant advantages in terms of privacy and performance for IoT infrastructures. However, deploying IDS on resource-limited Edge devices requires innovative solutions to ensure effective protection against cyber threats.By integrating IDS on IoT devices and strengthening security at Edge points, it becomes possible to effectively detect and mitigate malicious attacks while optimizing resource usage and ensuring the protection of sensitive data. By placing security at the core of IoT and Edge network design and deployment, it is possible to guarantee a robust and resilient infrastructure capable of addressing both current and future security challenges.This paper focuses on the study and implementation of machine learning algorithms applied to Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) within IoT networks. Specifically, we explore the use of real-world data IOT-23 dataset to improve the detection capabilities of IDS. The results show that boosting models, such as XGBoost, CatBoost, and Gradient Boosting, as well as Random Forests, deliver the highest performance with an F1-score of 0.84. These models demonstrate strong capabilities in detecting intrusions while maintaining an ideal balance between precision and recall. These results underscore the effectiveness of these algorithms in improving the security of IoT and Edge networks, paving the way for innovative strategies that allow for optimal resource utilization while ensuring robust protection of sensitive data.

articleTitle: Arabic Speech Recognition for Industrial Commands: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The integration of speech recognition technology in industrial environments has significantly enhanced humanmachine interaction, offering hands-free control over machinery in complex and noisy settings. This review focuses on the application of speech recognition for industrial command systems, with a particular emphasis on stochastic approaches such as Hidden Markov Models and their extensions. We examine the challenges posed by noisy environments, linguistic variability, and dialectal diversity, especially in Arabic, as well as the opportunities offered by advanced methods like deep learning. The paper also highlights emerging hybrid models that combine traditional and modern techniques to improve accuracy and robustness. Finally, the review outlines future research directions for optimizing speech recognition in industrial settings.

articleTitle: Disturbance Management-Based Finite-Time Adaptive Sliding Mode Control for Agriculture Mobile Robot: A Fixed-Time Observer-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: In the agriculture field, robotic systems are inevitably subject to multiple disturbances. This paper addresses critical challenges in managing disturbances in nonlinear systems like the Wheeled Mobile Robot (WMR). For this purpose, a Fixed-Time Extended State Observer (FxT-ESO) is designed. It aims to estimate different types of disturbances in a fixed time regardless of their initial values. Then, this observer is embedded in a closed-loop Finite-Time Adaptive Sliding Mode Controller (FT-ASMC). This later enables compensation for disturbances while avoiding the chattering problem thanks to the gain adjustment strategy. The simulation results show that this objective is achieved.

articleTitle: Towards Resource Efficient and Low Latency CNN Accelerator for FPGAs: Review and Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have seen widespread adoption in various domains, including speech recognition, image classification, and segmentation. However, their computational demands necessitate dedicated and reconfigurable hardware architectures, such as FieldProgrammable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). Despite the numerous advantages of CNN accelerators including enhanced efficiency within diverse application contexts, their deployment on FPGAs must address challenges related to energy consumption, computational demands, and resource optimization. Both academia and industries are actively engaged in research and development aimed at designing resource-efficient and lowlatency CNN accelerators for FPGAs. However, there has been relatively little attention paid to the dynamic comprehensive analysis and evaluation in which CNN accelerators equipped with FPGAs operate. This paper aims to bridge this gap by conducting a comprehensive survey and evaluation of CNN accelerator techniques for FPGAs, focusing on resource utilization, latency, and power consumption. This study investigates the performance of CNN accelerators for FPGAs, considering a range of hardware architectures and optimization techniques, from multiplier designs to complex heterogeneous pipelining. Furthermore, the paper highlights the challenges faced by FPGA-based CNN accelerators, particularly the tradeoffs between resource utilization and latency, based on the characteristics of the data and devices involved. The insights gleaned from this review can offer valuable guidance and inspiration to researchers, engineers, and students working in these domains, facilitating further advancements in FPGAbased CNN accelerator technology.

articleTitle: Ultra-Low Power DNN-based TSCH Scheduling at the Edge using the MAX78000
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The optimization of Time-Synchronized Channel Hopping (TSCH) scheduling at the edge plays a critical role in enhancing the efficiency and reliability of the Internet of Things (IoT). In this paper, we propose an approach leveraging Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) for TSCH scheduling. Our approach aims to harness the capabilities of hardware accelerators such as the MAX78000 to achieve efficient and reliable scheduling. We train a DNN using a database generated with the Traffic Aware Scheduling Algorithm (TASA) and evaluate its performance in generating schedules, achieving an accuracy of over 94%. Our experiments demonstrate significant reductions in execution time, with the DNN-based approach achieving an average reduction of 99.69% compared to running TASA on the same microcontroller. Similarly, a substantial reduction in energy consumption is observed, with the DNN-based approach consuming only 5 μJ compared to 1,606 μJ by TASA running in software. This represents a significant milestone in the field low-power wireless networks, as it opens up new possibilities for implementing sophisticated AI solutions directly on edge devices, without the need for extensive computational resources.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Techniques for Enhanced Classification of Gastrointestinal Images
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Deep learning has revolutionized medical image analysis, particularly in the classification of gastrointestinal abnormalities. This paper proposes a classification model based on an ensemble learning approach, combining three Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures: VGG16, DenseNet121, and InceptionV3. We first trained each model independently, then reused them with pre-trained weights from ImageNet to enhance performance. The outputs of the three models are concatenated to create a unified feature vector, which is then used for final classification through fully connected layers. This model was tested on the HyperKvasir dataset, a benchmark in gastrointestinal imaging. Our results demonstrate that using pretrained weights significantly improves accuracy compared to training from scratch, highlighting the effectiveness of the ensemble approach and pre-training in medical image classification.

articleTitle: Digital advancements in hypertension management
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Hypertension (HTN) is a significant global health crisis with rising prevalence, yet current management strategies often fall short. Traditional office-based care models often fall short in managing the condition effectively. Our literature review highlights the potential of digital health interventions, such as wearable devices and telemedicine, to enhance HTN care through continuous monitoring, early detection, and personalised treatment plans. While these technologies offer promise, their implementation requires careful consideration of ethical implications, including privacy, data quality, and fairness. To maximise their impact, addressing challenges related to accessibility, usability, and cost-effectiveness is crucial. Rigorous evaluation of the long-term benefits and sustainability of these digital solutions is essential for their successful integration into routine care.

articleTitle: Crop Yield Prediction in IoT: A Hybrid Feature Selection Approach using Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a pivotal technology applied across various domains such as smart homes, innovative healthcare, and smart farming. Despite its potential, IoT-based devices face major challenges, especially in combating crop diseases, addressing unpredictable weather patterns, and predicting crop yields. Traditional approaches predict crop yields often struggle with accuracy and reliability under environmental conditions. This study aims to increase predictive accuracy in an IoT environment by developing a hybrid feature selection method based on the Wrapper method. Therefore, we use advanced Machine Learning (ML) techniques like Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) for crop yield prediction. The proposed system was evaluated using multiple performance metrics, demonstrating that the hybrid method improved classification accuracy by approximately $4 \%$ more. Evaluation of KNN and AdaBoost algorithms ensures AdaBoost’s superior accuracy of $\mathbf{9 4 \%}$ and reliability of $\mathbf{9 5 \%}$. Simulation results highlight the efficiency of our approach in comparison to current practices, promising significant improvements in farming decision-making and sustainability measures.

articleTitle: Addressing Unhappiness in Elderly Care: Challenges in Causal AI and Span Categorization Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Causal Artificial Intelligence (AI) represents a transformative advancement in AI research, focusing on the identification and understanding of cause-and-effect relationships between variables. Unlike traditional AI, which primarily identifies patterns and correlations, causal AI aims to explain how specific events influence one another. This study explores the application of causal AI in Natural Language Processing (NLP) to develop a model capable of extracting the root causes of unhappiness among elderly residents in retirement homes from dialogue data.Our research reveals that the current state of causal AI in NLP is insufficient for effectively identifying these root causes. Consequently, we employed an alternative approach using span categorization, which allowed for a more precise analysis of textual spans within dialogues. This paper outlines our methodologies, from the initial exploration of causal AI to the challenges encountered and the eventual shift to span categorization.Our findings highlight current limitations in causal AI for NLP applications and offer insights into practical solutions for understanding the emotional states of elderly individuals through dialogue analysis. This work contributes to the broader field of AI-driven social support systems and underscores the need for further advancements in causal AI to fully realize its potential in complex NLP tasks.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Embedded Techniques for Biomedical Sentiment Analysis: Insights into Pandemic Drug-Related Issues on Social Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Modelling real-world phenomena involves complex networks. Sentiment Analysis has fared extremely well in identifying breakpoints in health-related public opinions. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, tremendous online patient narratives have poured on various platforms, characterized by hyperactivity, unprecedented dynamism to the global virus-fighting, and spreading massive related-medication information, e.g. common drugs used and their minute reactions. In this study, our objective is to perform a comparative analysis (1) of different embedding techniques in analyzing patients’ self-reports and (2) therefore Explore News of Drug-related Glitches. Various medical entities and related medication reports are effectively linked and semantically contextualized in diverse settings. As many examples of based-deep learning sentiment services are becoming highly reliable, few approaches succeed in analyzing medication-related narratives and seeking relevant sentimental insights towards medication aspects. Subsequently, we present a novel word representation taxonomy, which improves model reliability and leverages the different conceptual and contextual distributed insights by incorporating unlabelled data into the training process from online examples. The embedding gain is discussed, compared, and improved regarding the phenomena setting, which also incorporates data from highly controlled medical vocabularies, leading to a new hybrid model. The qualification of the proposed taxonomy for sentiment inference has been examined through many experiments on various dataset groups. The results of this study provide a useful resource for researchers and healthcare practitioners, facilitating the effective analysis of patient narratives within real-world contexts.

articleTitle: An innovative Federated Learning paradigm for safeguarding privacy in IoT through a synergistic SDN-CLOUD Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: As global society increasingly transitions towards a comprehensive dependence on computational systems and digitization, the formulation of secure environments and connections emerges as one of the foremost challenges of this decade. The proliferation of threats confronting both individuals and organizations is escalating at an exponential rate, attributable to the burgeoning intricacy of contemporary networks and the ascendance of the Internet of Things. Insufficient collaboration engenders a scenario wherein identical attacks are executed against disparate organizations in rapid succession. The dissemination of cyber threat intelligence is frequently proposed as a remedy to this predicament; however, it introduces distinct constraints pertaining to Data Safeguarding, traceability, and Integrity. To address this issue, a novel distributed architecture is put forth to augment the protective measures within the IoT landscape. This solution is predicated on federated learning algorithms aimed at constructing a distributed, self-governing system able to Identify intrusion and breaches through a synergistic SDNCloud Structure. This structural paradigm leverages the potential of SDN and cloud computing for IoT endpoints to enable effective and adaptable data analysis while concurrently maintaining user confidentiality. The adoption of federated learning simplifies a non-centralized model learning workflow, reducing data exposure and infringements by keeping private information confined to the IoT endpoints. Consequently, this methodology not only bolsters security but also promotes interdevice cooperation to confront the challenges in an exponentially interconnected.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning for Severity and Stages Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a frequent consequence linked to diabetes mellitus, characterized by progressive damage to the retina that can result in visual impairment and, if not detected and addressed promptly, can lead to blindness. Depending on its severity, DR can be categorized into four stages, from mild to proliferative. The diagnosis of DR is typically based on the analysis of retinal photographs, a procedure that may be complex, lengthy, and susceptible to mistakes. The design of an automated solution for DR detection could be a helpful and interesting solution for accelerated diagnosis and improved accuracy. In this article, an artificial intelligence-based method using the powerful Deep learning models, VGG-16 and ResNet-50, leveraging the power of transfer learning, is proposed to detect DR into five categories: no DR, mild NPDR, moderate NPDR, severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR), and proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR). An appropriate preprocessing chain has been first developed to improve retinal image quality. The data augmentation technique is then applied to enhance the amount of training data, improve model resilience, and reduce overfitting. Three separate datasets—APTOS, EyePACS, and IDRiD have been chosen to evaluate the proposed approach. The results are very promising; in fact when the developed model was fine-tuned. VGG-16 achieved an accuracy of $\mathbf{8 8 . 2 3 \%}$, while ResNet- 50 obtained a score of $\mathbf{8 7 . 7 4 \%}$. These findings emphasize the relevance and reliability of our proposed method for a precise classification of diabetic retinopathy stages, offering promising prospects for its future integration into innovative ophthalmological clinical applications.

articleTitle: A Systematic Review and Taxonomy of Ransomware Detection Based on Artificial Intelligence Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The escalating prevalence of ransomware attacks poses a significant risk to digital infrastructures, data integrity, and essential services worldwide. Traditional signature-based detection methods often struggle to keep pace with the evolving landscape of ransomware variants and stealthy attack techniques. Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers a promising solution, leveraging sophisticated features such as bytecodes, opcodes, API calls, and behavioral analysis to enhance ransomware detection capabilities. This review delves into the latest advancements in ransomware prevention and detection techniques, categorizing ransomware types and examining the intricate lifecycle of ransomware attacks. A comprehensive taxonomy of ransomware analysis techniques, machine/deep learning methods, and feature selection techniques is presented, considering the diverse operating systems targeted by these malicious threats. By conducting a thorough analysis of recent research articles in this field, we identify the key challenges faced by academics and the research community in mitigating the ransomware threat. Moreover, we explore potential future research directions to address these challenges and develop more effective countermeasures.

articleTitle: Build an efficient Amazigh Speech Recognition using a CNN-CTC model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This work focuses on the potential of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) in combination with Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) to develop an efficient Amazigh recognition system. The CNN-CTC model have a simple architecture, don’t need any alignment between the input and the output produces the most probable sequences of labels. In order to evaluate the performance of the model, a series of experiments were conducted. The experimental results demonstrate that the model attained a commendable accuracy of $93.5 \%$ when trained on a +30 -age category dataset with Dropout regularization.

articleTitle: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Employee Adaptability to Remote Work
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This empirical study looks at how XYZ organization, a financial services organization, is using artificial intelligence (AI) in remote work. This study examines the impact of AI tools, such Asana, Microsoft Teams, and Cortana, on employee satisfaction, productivity, and adaptability. According to the data, productivity increased significantly: Asana had improvements of $30 \%$, Microsoft Teams saw increases of $35 \%$, and Cortana saw gains of $10 \%$. While $20 \%$ of employees experience stress connected to technological change, the bulk of employees ($80 \%$) adjust to the new tools well. Regarding job satisfaction, $70 \%$ of workers say AI has improved their experience at work, while $30 \%$ are worried about greater surveillance and possible dehumanization of the workplace. The study comes to the conclusion that, even though artificial intelligence (AI) has a lot to offer in terms of productivity and satisfaction, it is essential to give workers enough support to help them adjust to new technologies and get past the difficulties that come with them.

articleTitle: Elevating Pulse Analysis: Variational and Empirical Mode Decomposition Algorithms for Heart Rate Extraction from Plethysmography Waves*
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This research emphasizes the use of advanced signal processing methods, including variational and empirical mode decomposition (VMD/EMD) techniques, to extract the instantaneous heart rate from photoplethysmogram (PPG) signals. Plethysmography is a non-invasive method widely used in healthcare for monitoring blood flow dynamics, and accurate heart rate estimation from plethysmography waveforms is crucial for various clinical applications. To improve heart rate extraction accuracy, especially during physical activities, we propose using adaptive decomposition techniques like VMD and EMD. These methods enable us to extract essential features from PPG signals by dividing them into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), which are vital for heart rate variability (HRV) analysis. We present a comparative analysis of the heart rate extraction outcomes obtained using the annotators from the BUT PPG database, EMD, and VMD approach. Our findings demonstrate a strong correlation between the heart rate extraction results, with a standard deviation of approximately 2.717 between the VMD technique and annotator 2. These results highlight the potential of these advanced signal processing techniques in enhancing heart rate estimation accuracy and contributing to more reliable assessments of cardiovascular health and other physiological aspects.

articleTitle: Contribution to Predicting Electricity Load using Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable energy solutions and the integration of renewable resources have increased the need for accurate electricity demand forecasting, which is an essential element in effective power system management. This study evaluates the application of the Random Forest (RF) algorithm, an ensemble learning technique, for predicting Short-Term Electricity Load (STEL). Using historical data including load, weather conditions, and calendar variables, we optimized the model through feature engineering and hyperparameter tuning, in an effort to capture the dynamic interactions between consumer behavior, climate effects, and seasonal patterns, all of which significantly influence electricity demand. The results demonstrate the RF model’s superiority over traditional methods, achieving high accuracy measured by Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Nonlinear System Identification: Kernels and ANN
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Modeling and identifying nonlinear systems are crucial challenges in many scientific and technical fields. This study examines the employment of machine learning for identifying non-linear systems, focusing specifically on two approaches: kernel methods and artificial neural networks (ANN). Kernel methods leverage nonlinear data transformations to model complex relationships by kernel trick, while ANN offers flexibility in modeling interactions between variables. We examine how these two approaches can effectively identify nonlinear systems output, highlighting their respective advantages and disadvantages. Case Experiments illustrate how well these methods perform across different system identification scenarios.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of intelligent Voice Disorder Diagnosis: Techniques, Databases, and Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The diagnosis and monitoring of voice-affecting disorders using machine learning (ML) approaches have garnered significant attention globally. This review highlights the current state of research in this domain, identifying a growing interest in leveraging ML techniques for voice disorder diagnosis. However, it reveals several limitations, such as the inconsistent use of datasets across studies and a predominant focus on diagnostic accuracy, often overlooking long-term surveillance of specific disorders. Despite these shortcomings, this review provides valuable insights into the potential of ML-based voice disorder detection and emphasizes the need for broader research efforts. Expanding access to diverse datasets and addressing disorder-specific monitoring will be crucial to advancing clinical applications in this field.

articleTitle: Development of an Explainable AI (XAI) system for the interpretation of ViT in the diagnosis of medical images
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: ViT for Vision Transformer have emerged as powerful deep learning architectures for medical image analysis, achieving performance in various diagnostic tasks. However, their complex internal mechanisms often hinder interpretability, limiting trust and hindering wider adoption in clinical applications. This study explores the development of an Explainable AI (XAI) system to interpret the decision-making process of a ViT model trained for skin lesion severity classification using the HAM10000 dataset. We leverage five explainability techniques —Attention Rollout, Beyond Attention, Generic Attention, Beyond Intuition, and Transition Attention Maps— to generate saliency maps, providing visual insights into the regions and features deemed most influential by the model for its predictions. Through saliency map visualizations, we demonstrate that the ViT model often learns to focus on clinically relevant features consistent with dermatological criteria, even without explicit feature annotations during training. However, the analyses also reveal potential biases, such as an over-reliance on color variations, and challenges in handling cases presenting with multiple diagnostic features. Our findings provide valuable insights for refining ViT models for skin lesion diagnosis and highlight the essential role of XAI in facilitating transparent and trustworthy AI-driven clinical applications.

articleTitle: Comparison of Traditional Tool Combination and Deep Learning Methods for Automatic Classification of Steel Surface Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: In industry, the automatic recognition of surface defects of flat steel products still represents a real challenge. Indeed, in addition to constraints such as the image noise or blur, there is neither an agreed standard of these defects, which can be of different sizes, shapes, orientations, and locations, nor a standard defect identification method, whether based on traditional tools such as statistical-based, spatial/frequency filtering based or model-based or on newer techniques such as deep learning. Hence, the complexity of the algorithm that deals with this matter always depends on the specific needs of the application. This paper focuses on the comparison of deep learning approaches with a new combination of traditional tools, namely the Gabor wavelets (GW) and the Local Phase Quantization, respectively known for image abrupt change representation and for the invariance to image blur. Both approaches are assessed on the North University (NEU) and a Research Center (RC_DDB) datasets, which include surface defect images of hot rolled steel product. Interesting correct-prediction rates and processing times are achieved for both approaches, with slightly higher scores for the Deep Learning approaches in terms of accuracy, but better computation times for the proposed combination.

articleTitle: Transformer-based Arabic language lemmatization
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Traditional morphological methods have long been at the heart of Arabic language processing. They exploit the complex morphological structure of the language, characterized by roots, prefixes, infixes, and suffixes used for analyzing and generating words. These methods have been effective for tasks such as lemmatization, and rooting. However, they can be resource-intensive and do not always take semantics into account. Recent advancements in deep learning, particularly transformer-based models, offer new prospects for Arabic language processing. Despite their success in languages such as Turkish, Latin, English, and Slavic, to our knowledge, no transformer-based method has been implemented for the Arabic lemmatization task. In this study, we propose a transformer-based lemmatizer using T5, specifically AraT5, MT5, and BERT. We evaluate the models using the ArabicPADT UD Treebank corpus and benchmark their performance against standard metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. Our results show an accuracy of $88.58 \%$, demonstrating competitive performance and highlighting the potential of transformer-based models for advancing Arabic lemmatization.

articleTitle: Improving the CXR Reports Generation with Multi-modal feature Alignment and Self-Refining strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
