abstract: Medical chest X-ray images are necessary for the diagnosis of different diseases. The need for automated interpretation and report generation of these images is crucial. It not only saves radiologists’ time but also minimizes the risk of diagnostic mistakes. However, several challenges impede this task due to the employment of uni-directional image-to-report in the encoder-decoder deep learning model and the absence of contextual details in the process of report generation can lead to incomplete or inaccurate descriptions. To address this, we propose an approach based on Multi-modal feature Alignment and Self-Refining mechanism RG-MASR in order to generate an improved medical report from chest X-ray images automatically. Our method comprises three modules: visual and textual characteristics extraction to extract the semantic characteristics from X-ray images and their paired reports. Second, a multimodal feature alignment module is employed to leverage both textual and visual features. Finally, we integrate a self-refining technique in the report generator module to refine alignment and improve the output to generate a comprehensive report. We evaluate our method on the IU X-ray and NIH public chest X-ray datasets. The results demonstrate that our proposed RG-MASR surpasses existing approaches in terms of ROUGE and BLEU metrics.

articleTitle: Refined Coati Optimizer with Chaotic Systems for Optimization in Image Processing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The Coati Optimization Algorithm (COA) is a promising metaheuristic inspired by coati hunting behaviors, demonstrating strong performance in complex optimization tasks. However, COA encounters challenges with convergence speed and is susceptible to getting trapped in local optima. This paper introduces the Refined Coati Optimizer (R-CO), an enhanced COA variant incorporating chaotic systems to improve exploration and exploitation phases. By embedding chaotic maps, R-CO increases search diversity, accelerates convergence, and reduces the likelihood of premature convergence. Extensive testing on 23 benchmark functions—covering unimodal, multimodal, and fixed-dimension multimodal problems—confirms the algorithm’s robust performance. $\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{CO}$ is also applied to an image segmentation task, where it outperforms the original COA and other leading metaheuristic algorithms. Results highlight R-CO’s enhanced optimization capabilities, positioning it as a valuable tool for theoretical and applied optimization challenges.

articleTitle: Image Clustering Approach based on Artificial Bee Colony and enhanced K-means algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Clustering plays a pivotal role in image segmentation by grouping pixels based on similarity, enabling efficient analysis and interpretation. Traditional methods like K-means, despite their popularity, are hindered by their sensitivity to initial centroid placement, often converging to suboptimal solutions. This paper presents a novel hybrid approach that integrates the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm with K-means to address these limitations. The proposed method leverages the global optimization capabilities of ABC to enhance centroid initialization, thereby improving clustering accuracy and robustness. The method was evaluated on benchmark image datasets, including Lenna, House, Baboon, and Elephants, using widely adopted metrics such as IoU, Precision, F1 Score, and Dice Coefficient. Results demonstrate consistent improvements across all datasets, with significant gains in accuracy compared to K-means, Fuzzy C-Means, and Mean Shift. Despite higher computational overhead, the proposed method exhibits superior segmentation quality, particularly in complex images with intricate structures. Future work aims to optimize the computational efficiency of the approach and explore its application in text clustering and time-series data analysis.

articleTitle: Towards a Question/Answering System in Moroccan Legal Domain: Investigation of the impact of tailored preprocessing techniques and alternative word representations on the question classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Automatic classification of Arabic legal questions is crucial for legal information retrieval and intelligent legal systems such as question-answering systems. However, the unique characteristics of Arabic legal text, including complex morphology and domain-specific terminology, pose challenges for accurate classification. This paper investigates the impact of preprocessing techniques and word representation on the performance of a legal question classification system. We propose a framework that utilizes various preprocessing techniques including cleaning, stop word removal, and stemming techniques tailored for Arabic legal text, along with word representation techniques. We assess the efficacy of various techniques on a dataset of Moroccan Arabic legal questions, examining the impact of different preprocessing combinations and word embedding strategies on classification accuracy using Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Random Forest algorithms. The experimental results reveal that the combination of N -gram features with Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency weighting (TF-IDF), when used with SVM, achieves the highest accuracy of $87.4 \%$. Furthermore, our findings underscore the significance of preprocessing in enhancing classification performance, with particular emphasis on the stemming step.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Diagnostic Framework for Hepatitis C Prediction Using Machine Learning with Advanced Feature Selection Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Hepatitis C is a major global health concern and one of the leading causes of chronic liver disease, liver cirrhosis, and liver cancer worldwide. In this paper, an intelligent machine-learning algorithm-based Hepatitis C diagnosis system has been proposed. A publicly available Hepatitis C dataset has been utilized to develop the prediction framework. The dataset shows a significant imbalance between positive and negative cases, which complicates the classification process, a common challenge in healthcare datasets. Appropriate strategies have been undertaken to achieve a reliable decision framework. Two feature selection techniques, Sequential Feature Selection (SFS) and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), were incorporated to identify the most representative set of attributes and improve the system’s diagnostic performance. Six different classifiers were employed for prediction, among which Adaboost with the SFS algorithm achieved the highest MCC score of $\mathbf{9 2. 6 \%}$, providing the most effective prediction of Hepatitis C. This framework offers a robust approach for early diagnosis, potentially benefiting patient care and optimizing healthcare resources.

articleTitle: Impact of Digital Resources on Learning Nuclear Physics A Case Study on Isotopes and Atomic Mass in Final Year High School Students
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This study evaluates the impact of digital resources on the learning of nuclear physics concepts among final-year high school students, particularly isotopes and atomic mass. The experimental group using digital tools showed significant improvement in knowledge acquisition compared to the control group after comparing post-test results and relative learning gains between the two groups. The results clearly demonstrated that students in the experimental group (taught with the digital resource) achieved better results and significantly higher learning gains than those in the control group (taught in a traditional manner). The findings indicate that the use of digital resources can have a considerable beneficial effect on students’ knowledge acquisition and improve their academic performance.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic hotspot fault detection based on detectron2 with faster R-CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Solar energy is widely recognised as one of the cleanest and most sustainable methods for harnessing sunlight into electricity. However, photovoltaic systems are susceptible to critical issues such as hotspots, often caused by various factors such as partial shading, short circuits or line-to-line faults. These issues can significantly diminish efficiency and lifespan, undermining the reliability and effectiveness of solar power generation. This study investigates the performance of various Faster R-CNN backbones within Detectron2 to determine the most effective architecture for detecting hotspots in photovoltaic panels through thermal imagery. After training each backbone individually, a systematic evaluation of the performance of each backbone architecture is undertaken, emphasising classification accuracy, loss convergence and performance metrics on the test set to get a complete insight into its efficiency. The model presented in this paper achieved an impressive ${9 8 \%}$ accuracy in foreground classification and an Average Precision at 50% Intersection over Union (AP50) of ${7 6. 5 8 \%}$. This approach demonstrates the potential of various Faster R-CNN backbones for real-time fault detection, supports proactive maintenance and enhances the efficiency and reliability of Photovoltaic systems.

articleTitle: Integrating Industry 4.0 into Moroccan Supply Chain Management: Technologies, Transformations, and Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: In the face of increasing global competition and rapid technological advancements, Industry 4.0 technologies like the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and big data analytics are redefining supply chain management (SCM). This paper examines the integration of these technologies into Moroccan SCM, highlighting their transformative impacts on efficiency, sustainability, and resilience. Through an empirical analysis and case studies in Moroccan industries, particularly automotive and aerospace, this study underscores the unique challenges and opportunities of adopting Industry 4.0 in emerging markets. The findings reveal that strategic planning and investments are crucial to leveraging these technologies fully, positioning Moroccan industries on a path towards global competitiveness. Future research directions and practical recommendations are also provided to support further advancements in this domain.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Techniques for Cardiovascular Disease Classification using 12-Lead ECG
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Cardiovascular disorders, including atrial fibrillation and bundle branch blockages, have a significant impact on global health and are associated with higher mortality rates. The accurate categorization of these disorders through ECG data is essential in order to improve the results for patients. This investigation addresses the challenge of classifying major cardiac conditions by utilizing seven ECG datasets and employing machine learning techniques. We seek to classify patients exhibiting atypical ECGs through advanced methodologies. We combined datasets, incorporating 12 leads, and utilized preprocessing techniques to enhance data quality. By employing various models, such as CNN, SVM, KNN, random forest, and logistic regression, our CNN combined with logistic regression attained an accuracy of $94 \%$ and a sensitivity of $94 \%$ on a test set comprising 1500 ECGs. This comprehensive approach minimizes false negatives and enhances diagnostic precision. The integration of multiple datasets and sophisticated preprocessing improves the dependability of our findings, highlighting the importance of data quality and comprehensive analysis in cardiac diagnostics. The results demonstrate how machine learning can improve cardiac diagnoses through thorough data integration and analysis.

articleTitle: Enhanced Hybrid Approach for Real-Time Emotion Recognition Using Canny Edge Detection and Deep Learning on Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to real-time emotion recognition, integrating Canny’s edge detection and deep learning on an embedded system, namely the Raspberry Pi 3 board. Our method combines the edge detection capabilities of the Canny algorithm with the robust feature extraction and analytical strengths of advanced deep learning techniques. The pre-processing phase involves applying Canny’s edge detection to highlight facial contours and important features, which are subsequently processed by a convolutional neural network (CNN) to determine emotional states. This hybrid approach improves the accuracy of emotion recognition, enabling real-time application on resource-constrained devices. Extensive experiments on reference datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in real time. This work opens up new perspectives for developing portable and efficient emotion recognition systems for applications in healthcare, and surveillance.

articleTitle: Review of 3D Scene Reconstruction: From Traditional Methods to Advanced Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: 3D scene reconstruction represents a pivotal domain within computer vision, involving a diverse array of techniques ranging from classical geometry-driven approaches to modern deep learning-based models. This review article offers an extensive summary of cutting-edge methods for 3D reconstruction, including techniques such as Structure-from-Motion (SfM) and Multi-View Stereo (MVS), as well as cutting-edge deep learning techniques including CNNs, GANs,Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF). We analyze the strengths and limitations of each approach, particularly in terms of accuracy, efficiency, generalization, and their ability to handle complex scenes. Furthermore, we delve into the key challenges faced in 3D scene reconstruction, including the trade-offs between computational efficiency and model accuracy, the generalization to diverse environments, and the integration of multi-modal data sources. Special attention is given to NeRF, a breakthrough in the field, discussing its current capabilities and potential areas for improvement in future research. This review aims to serve as a resource for researchers and practitioners by summarizing the current landscape of 3D reconstruction technologies and identifying promising directions for future exploration.

articleTitle: New Biometric Recognition System By Multichannel Orthogonal Radial Triangular Pulse Moments
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: Biometrics involves measuring biological characteristics to identify or authenticate individuals based on specific traits. A biometric system functions by capturing biometric data, extracting relevant features, and comparing these with stored data in a database. Depending on the medium used, biometric systems can focus on various characteristics such as iris patterns, facial features, fingerprints, or signatures. These systems employ various feature extraction techniques to facilitate recognition. This study presents a performance analysis of reconstruction and classification using K-Nearest Neighbors with $k=1$ (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and multichannel orthogonal radial triangular pulse moment invariants. Additionally, the performance of the proposed invariant feature vectors for biometric recognition is evaluated by numerical experimental experiments. Finally, by comparing our methods with real-time static characteristics, we demonstrate their potential efficacy in accurately recognizing patterns, highlighting their applicability within the field of biometric systems.

Author Keywords: multichannel radial orthogonal triangular pulse moments

articleTitle: Li-Fi in medical applications
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Embedded Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI)
abstract: The advent of more powerful and faster light-emitting diodes (LEDs) has led to the idea of using them as information transmitters. The light emitted by LEDs becomes a wireless communication channel, allowing applications indoors and, in some cases, outdoors. This technology is known as “Li-Fi”. With the spread of the COVID-19 virus, the world is on high alert. In hospitals, patients in intensive care units must be closely monitored at all times, as they require specialised equipment to maintain normal bodily functions. The challenge lies in the ability to monitor each patient while maintaining the confidentiality of their information, in this article we will talk about Li-Fi technology, we will also propose a new Li-Fi diagram. We will give examples of the use of Li-Fi in hospitals and finally, we will give a conclusion of the article.
